title: Priyanka Chopra Adds Angelina Jolie to a Slate That Already Has Rajamouli, Mira Nair and Orlando Bloom. The Desi Queen Is Building an Empire.
excerpt: She came up taking scripts no one wrote for her. Now she's picking and choosing — and quietly assembling the most globe-spanning year any Indian actress has ever had.
body:
There's a particular kind of power that only arrives once you stop asking permission. Priyanka Chopra Jonas has it now, and she said the quiet part out loud.

"When I started, scripts were not customized for me," she told Fortune India this week. "My husband Nick recently said, 'You are on the other side of your sacrifice.' I can now pick and choose and create my own projects."

Read that line twice, because it reframes everything that follows. The girl from Jamshedpur who won Miss World in 2000, who fought for every Hollywood door in an era when there were no doors for women who looked like her, is now the one deciding which rooms are worth walking into. And the rooms she's chosen for 2026 and 2027 read like a fever dream pinned to a diaspora kid's bedroom wall.

https://x.com/SacnilkEntmt/status/2068280006888022193

!Mira Nair — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

""When I started, scripts were not customized for me," she told Fortune India this week."

The headline this week: an as-yet-undefined collaboration with Angelina Jolie. Chopra confirmed it without disclosing whether it's a film, a campaign, or a philanthropic venture — the kind of strategic non-answer that keeps the internet refreshing. What she did offer was reverence. She named Jolie, alongside Penelope Cruz and Salma Hayek, as women whose careers she finds genuinely inspiring. Coming from someone who has spent a decade being the inspiration, that's a telling tribute — one global force acknowledging another, peer to peer, no longer fan to idol.

But the Jolie news lands hardest when you set it inside the rest of her calendar, because the scale is almost absurd.

First, the homecoming. After seven years away from Indian cinema, Chopra returns in Varanasi, directed by SS Rajamouli — the man who made RRR a global phenomenon and turned an Oscar stage into a Telugu victory lap. Varanasi is being mounted as one of the most expensive Indian films ever made, with a budget reportedly between ₹1,200 and ₹1,400 crore (roughly $135–150 million). They shot it across Georgia, Antarctica, Africa and Hyderabad — an actual globe-trotting adventure, not a green-screen approximation of one.

"What we are trying to do is something so ambitious and of a scale not seen for a very long time." — Priyanka Chopra Jonas

!Orlando Bloom — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

That's not marketing bluster from a publicist. That's the star herself, and given who's directing, you believe her. Varanasi opens worldwide on April 7, 2027.

Then there's the prestige play. Chopra joins Mira Nair's Amri, the long-gestating biopic of the trailblazing painter Amrita Sher-Gil — herself a cross-cultural icon, born in Budapest to a Hungarian mother and a Sikh father, who fused European oil technique with the soul of rural India before dying at just 28. Chopra plays Madame Azurie and serves as executive producer, marking her first collaboration with Nair, the woman who gave us Monsoon Wedding and The Namesake. Two of the most globally fluent Indian women in the business, finally in the same frame. For the diaspora, whose entire identity is the art of blending two worlds, a Sher-Gil film made by Nair and produced by Chopra is almost too on-the-nose. We'll take it.

And the Hollywood ledger keeps filling. She's set to star opposite Orlando Bloom in a co-production, and she turns up in Nicholas Stoller's comedy Judgment Day alongside Will Ferrell, Zac Efron and Regina Hall. A Rajamouli epic, a Mira Nair art film, an Orlando Bloom two-hander, a studio comedy, and whatever the Jolie project becomes. Name another Indian actor — of any gender — running that spread at once.

What makes this moment land is the deliberateness of it. Chopra isn't chasing volume; she's curating a legacy. Every project is a different muscle: the four-quadrant Indian blockbuster, the international auteur drama, the glossy Hollywood ensemble. She's not picking between Bombay and Los Angeles anymore. She refuses the choice entirely, and she's earned the right to.

For NRIs watching from Edison, Hounslow or Brampton, that refusal is the whole point. We've spent our lives being asked to choose a side. Chopra built a career out of choosing both, then made both come to her. The Jolie collaboration is the cherry — but the cake underneath is a year that proves a desi woman can stand at the absolute centre of global cinema and direct traffic.

The sacrifice, as Nick said, is behind her. What's in front looks like an empire.
